Look-alike ages, heights and checks from the Before You Drive pages, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A01
The front-seat belt rule covers every front seat occupant of any age, while the driver's duty to make passengers buckle up covers every passenger under 16. [A01]
Why it matters: group safety belts; difficulty two; confusable sec04-F09 versus sec04-F11.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A01
Seat, steering wheel and mirrors are adjusted before you start the vehicle, while the turn signal and brake check is the step before you put it in motion. [A01]
Why it matters: group preparation; difficulty two; confusable sec04-F03 versus sec04-F04.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A01
Tire pressure is checked against the vehicle's recommended psi on the door jamb, while tread depth is checked with the penny test; one is about air, the other about wear. [A01]
Why it matters: group tires; difficulty one; confusable sec04-F07 versus sec04-F08.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A02
Under 5 a child restraint is always required, but from 5 to 8 the restraint is required only until the child reaches 4 feet 9 inches. [A02]
Why it matters: group child restraints; difficulty three; confusable sec04-F15 versus sec04-F16.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A02
Car-seat ages stop at 8, but the front-seat warning reaches higher: children 12 and under should never ride in front because air bags are unsafe for them. [A02]
Why it matters: group child restraints; difficulty two; confusable sec04-F16 versus sec04-F20.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A02
The lap belt prevents ejection and protects the lower body, while the shoulder belt protects the head and chest from the dashboard and windshield. [A02]
Why it matters: group safety belts; difficulty one; prereq sec04-F13.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A02
With several children under 8, the rule is to secure as many as reasonably fit given the passenger area and passenger count, rather than a fixed number of seats. [A02]
Why it matters: group child restraints; difficulty three; prereq sec04-F18.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A03
Cars and trucks need two separate brake systems, a foot brake and a parking brake, each acting on at least two wheels, while a motorcycle needs only one brake worked by hand or foot. [A03]
Why it matters: group brakes; difficulty two; confusable sec04-F32 versus sec04-F33.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A03
A failed emission inspection opens a 30-day window to fix the problem and come back for a follow-up re-check. [A03]
Why it matters: group vehicle upkeep; difficulty one; prereq sec04-F29.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A03
The secured-load rule applies to any vehicle on a highway, street or roadway, and covers loads that drop, sift or leak as well as any other way a load can escape. [A03]
Why it matters: group loads; difficulty two; prereq sec04-F31.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A03
The 511 line and az511.com are free ADOT services, so checking road conditions before a trip costs nothing. [A03]
Why it matters: group travel information; difficulty one; prereq sec04-F26.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0021]
